question: Does the message present an unexpected benefit, opportunity, reward, or entitlement for the recipient?
Does the message mention competitions, draws, claims, vouchers, credits, bonuses, or similar promotional incentives?
Does the message use a sales-like pitch for a service, product, subscription, dating line, entertainment, or content access?
Does the message suggest exclusivity, selection, eligibility, membership, VIP status, or special access?
Does the message mention currency amounts, cash, credit, loans, winnings, compensation, or financial value?
Does the message mention charges, fees, billing, balance, tariff, premium rate, or subscription cost?
Does the message mention saving money, discounts, cheap rates, reduced prices, or special deals?
Does the message mention bank, account, payment card, transaction, refund, or account status?
Does the message impose a time limit, deadline, expiry, final reminder, or limited availability?
Does the message pressure the recipient by warning of loss, cancellation, suspension, or missed opportunity?
Does the message ask the recipient to confirm, validate, activate, claim, register, or verify something?
Does the message give a keyword, code, PIN, reference number, or instruction token for the recipient to use?
Does the message contain or refer to a website, URL, email address, online form, or app link?
Does the message include a phone number, short code, service number, or other contact endpoint?
Does the message mention opt-out, stop instructions, terms, conditions, customer care, or subscription management?
Does the message appear to come from a company, operator, service, institution, or automated notification?
Does the message refer to shared plans, daily logistics, errands, travel, meals, school, work, family, or friends?
Does the message depend on prior shared context, such as "see you", "call me", "I told you", or ongoing conversation?
Does the message use informal affection, teasing, apology, humor, greetings, or personal emotional language?
Does the message mainly coordinate a real-world personal action rather than advertise, verify, or sell something?
